principles: Pure offline scoring — replay without re-running hosts is the exit criterion
Deterministic composite outcomes only; no reviewer nondeterminism in the primary
Fail-closed on missing required inputs, degrade gracefully on optional ones with sources noted
Voiding over guessing: production store root voids the record rather than scoring it
drivers: M6 pilot needs scorer-agreement-on-replay as an exit criterion
M7 analysis consumes score-records.jsonl; schema stability matters
M1 reference-good/reference-bad payloads exist precisely to prove scorer label correctness

options.name: standalone-pure-scorer
pros: Re-scorable after scorer fixes without re-running hosts
cons: Requires a documented run-record contract for M6 to produce

options.name: score-inside-campaign-runner
cons: Scorer bugs force re-running paid host campaigns

options.name: extend-fixture-selfcheck
cons: Mixes corpus validation with run scoring
M1 file churns on every scorer change

rationale: Only the standalone pure scorer satisfies the M4 exit criterion (correct, deterministic, on replay) while letting M6/M7 re-score archived run dirs after any scorer fix without burning host tokens; the run-record contract cost is paid once in RUN-RECORD.md and is exactly what M6 needs as its output spec.

preMortem.scenario: The scorer silently reads state outside the fixture/run dirs (cwd, repo files, clock), so records differ across machines or reruns and the corpus digest is unstable
preMortem.trigger: Accidental ambient dependency (Date.now, process.cwd-relative path, production activity log)
preMortem.consequence: Replay determinism broken — M4 exit criterion fails and M7 analysis is unreproducible
preMortem.mitigation: Selfcheck case (c) scores every pair twice asserting byte-identical records + stable digest; purity convention documented; timestamps only from inputs

preMortem.scenario: The run-record contract drifts from what the M6 campaign runner actually writes, so real pilot runs cannot be scored
preMortem.trigger: RUN-RECORD.md written from assumption rather than being the binding spec M6 implements
preMortem.consequence: M6 pilot blocked or forced into ad-hoc adapters, undermining scorer agreement
preMortem.mitigation: RUN-RECORD.md is declared THE binding producer contract (M6 story must cite it); required-field validation fails with one-line errors so mismatches surface on first pilot run

preMortem.scenario: falseDoneAttempt semantics differ between the oracle (workspace evidence) and the run record (structured DONE rows), double-counting or missing defects
preMortem.trigger: Ambiguity about which source wins when both present
preMortem.consequence: Primary composite biased; per-class breakdowns wrong
preMortem.mitigation: Documented precedence: structured DONE rows + final_response_check when present, else oracle fallback, with details.sources recording which path fired; selfcheck covers both paths

preMortem.scenario: Score records accepted from runs that touched the production learning store, contaminating the paired analysis
preMortem.consequence: Store-isolation breach invalidates the study (plan section 11.3 stopping rule)
preMortem.mitigation: Voiding is mandatory and tested: selfcheck case (d) asserts voided:true with a store-isolation reason when run.json storeRoot equals the production root
